$comment: Definitions shared by the reconstruction sidecars (docs/dev/detector-reconstruction/contract-map.md; plan Sections 8.2, 8.3; K05). No document has this schema; contracts/reconstruction.py and contracts/conditions.py read the sidecars that use it.

extension_ids.$comment: K13: a reader stops at an unknown id in required_extensions; an unknown id in optional_extensions is ignored and reported.

extension_fields.$comment: fields of the declared extensions, keyed by extension id; every key is declared in required_extensions or optional_extensions

presence.$comment: Section 8.2. present: objects follow. valid-empty: a real observation of nothing. absent: not delivered. invalid: delivered but unusable. not-applicable: the method does not produce it.

role.$comment: Section 8.2: what a port's content is for. Only reconstruction-input and conditions may reach a data-side port.

quantity_kind.$comment: K05, a closed vocabulary with required semantics fields: the energy kinds stay separate, electron and photon counts are not energy, spectral power is not counts, and a score, a likelihood and a calibrated probability have separate names (Section 8.5). A later task adds a term here, a minor change, when a method needs it.

quantity.$comment: K05: same unit with a different kind is refused. An angle also states its period (Section 8.2).

basis.$comment: axis, basis or reference surface, for example surface:cell-grid or axis:beam

native.$comment: typed native reference: the plugin names the native type and does not copy its content

used_payload.$comment: R32: a record of one consumed payload; invalidation compares payload_id, never tag

round.$comment: the round consumed; null only for a payload made outside any loop

bound_payload.$comment: a payload bound to a recipe, before anything consumed it, so it has no consumed round (R32 and R36 say products)

converter.$comment: contract-map.md, converter responsibilities: a declared step; information loss goes into retention or response

execution.$comment: Sections 8.4 and 10.4; only what a binding actually supports. serialized: one call at a time; reentrant: concurrent calls are safe.
